newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises to 14/15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises to 14/15 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 14/15 percent on Friday morning from around 11/12 percent at the opening on the back of tight rupiah liquidity, dealers said.

One local bank dealer said the early central bank injection of 1.666 trillion rupiah helped capped the rate from rising further despite higher demand due to tax payments and the end of reporting period.
"Some state-owned banks were seen buying rupiah minutes after the opening, pushing the rates briefly to 16 percent before they eased to around 14/15 percent," the bank dealer said.
The central bank offered one-week SBIs at 11.25 percent, two-week at 11.50 percent, one-month at 12.50 percent, three-month at 13.25 percent, six-month at 13.50 percent and 12-month at 13.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate was 10.73 percent on Thursday compared with 11.61 percent on Wednesday.
